text:
Bitcoin collapsed to $61,860 the late afternoon of June 23, finalizing a brutal 5% intraday drawdown that triggered over $575 million in long liquidations. This digital asset rout is inextricably linked to a severe tech equity rotation, as capital aggressively exits semiconductor and AI high-flyers on the Nasdaq. Institutional crypto allocators have exacerbated the downside, driving a staggering $8 billion in net outflows across major ETFs over the past 30 days.

Amid the spot market carnage, institutional regulatory infrastructure is rapidly advancing. Bitcoin Suisse secured a critical MiCAR-compliant CASP license in Liechtenstein ahead of the July 1 deadline, while Dubai's VARA framework prepares to onboard Atlas Capital's new regulated security, USAFi.

This correlated crypto-equity drawdown is fundamentally dictated by restrictive global liquidity. With Canadian inflation unexpectedly accelerating to 3.2% and the 2-year U.S. Treasury yield surging above 4.2%, the prospect of an imminent Federal Reserve rate hike is aggressively draining risk-asset momentum.
